business.explanation:
The baseline failed with TypeError at the line calling `_actions(state, types, links)` because `_actions` was declared with only two parameters. Fixed by declaring `links` as a third parameter and passing the already-computed link map.

I also removed the dead `_LINK_CACHE` (keyed on `id(types)`, which is unsound since ids are recycled across objects) and the `_compute_links` stub that always returned `{}`; the link relation is read directly from the init facts in `get_plan`, so the cache added nothing. Removed the no-op `out.add("locatable") if False else None` line and the unused `_subtypes`/`_applicable` helpers, which were never called.

I left the unknown-goal-predicate behavior in `_goal_satisfied` unchanged (it returns False, making such goals unsatisfiable) and only corrected the comment to describe the actual behavior, since I have no evidence about which semantics the evaluator expects and changing search behavior is not required by the observed failure. The `steps > 200000` truncation guard is likewise unchanged.

Scope note: this addresses the reported Python exception only. It does not establish task success on the diagnostics, and the two public examples were not executed here.
